collection: NCEE Verbal Aptitude: homonyms in context
note: Original four-option practice for final-year primary pupils. The historical topic reference is provisional. Independent academic review pending.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “The pupils put the seed packets in a tin.” Which sentence uses “tin” in the same sense?
questions.answer: Musa lifted the lid of a tin and took out some buttons.
options: Musa lifted the lid of a tin and took out some buttons.
The label says the wire contains tin.
The workers melt tin before combining it with another metal.
The class saw a sample of tin in the display of metals.
questions.explanation: Here “tin” refers to a container. The other examples use it to name a metal.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: Complete both sentences with the same word. “The nurse put a clean strip of cloth over the ____.” “The drummer ____ the cord around the handle.”
options: strap
wound
wrapped
cut
questions.explanation: In the first sentence “wound” is an injury. In the second it is the past tense of “wind”, meaning to wrap or coil.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “The children watched a bat fly out from under the roof.” Which clue tells you what “bat” means here?
questions.answer: It flew out from under the roof.
options: There were several children.
The children were watching.
It flew out from under the roof.
The sentence mentions a roof.
questions.explanation: A bat that flies out by itself is an animal. The roof alone does not distinguish it from a piece of sports equipment stored there.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: Which pair uses “seal” with two different meanings?
questions.answer: “We saw a seal swimming.” / “Press the lid down to seal the jar.”
options: “Seal the envelope after signing.” / “Use tape to seal the parcel.”
“A seal dived for fish.” / “We watched a seal climb onto a rock.”
“Seal the gap around the pipe.” / “Seal the opening with wax.”
“We saw a seal swimming.” / “Press the lid down to seal the jar.”
questions.explanation: The first use names an animal. The second means to close an opening securely.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “Zainab can conduct the choir on Friday.” Which meaning of “conduct” fits the situation?
questions.answer: Direct the singers as they perform.
options: Direct the singers as they perform.
Carry heat through a material.
Behave in a particular way.
Carry out a survey.
questions.explanation: A person who conducts a choir directs its singers, giving cues such as when to begin or end.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: Read the sentences. “A crane lifted the water tank onto the stand.” “A crane stood at the edge of the pond.” What helps you tell the two meanings apart?
questions.answer: The first crane lifts a heavy load, while the second has the behaviour of a living creature.
options: The first crane is farther from the speaker than the second.
The first crane lifts a heavy load, while the second has the behaviour of a living creature.
The first crane is newer than the second.
The first crane belongs to someone, while the second does not.
questions.explanation: The heavy lift points to a machine. Standing at a pond is consistent with the bird called a crane.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses “bark” to mean a covering?
questions.answer: The gardener examined the bark on the young tree.
options: The sharp bark woke the neighbours.
The guard dog began to bark when the van arrived.
The gardener examined the bark on the young tree.
The coach gave a bark of laughter.
questions.explanation: A tree’s bark is its outer covering. The other examples refer to short, sharp sounds.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “Please train the new library helpers.” Which sentence uses “train” with the same meaning?
questions.answer: The caretaker will train the team to use the new equipment.
options: We caught the morning train at the station.
The bride lifted the train of her dress off the muddy path.
A train of carts left the festival ground.
The caretaker will train the team to use the new equipment.
questions.explanation: To train people is to teach them how to perform a task. The other meanings describe things that follow in a line.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: Complete both sentences with the same word. “The farmer gathered the goats into a ____ before dark.” “Nneka signed the card with a blue ____.”
options: pen
gate
post
pencil
questions.explanation: A pen is an enclosure for animals or an instrument used to write with ink.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “The flour was weighed on a scale.” Which sentence uses “scale” to mean something different?
questions.answer: The key says the map is drawn to a scale of one centimetre to one kilometre.
options: Chika put the bag of beans on the market scale.
The key says the map is drawn to a scale of one centimetre to one kilometre.
The vendor set the empty scale to zero.
The cook checked the amount of rice on the kitchen scale.
questions.explanation: In the drawing, scale is a ratio of sizes. A scale used to weigh flour or rice is a measuring instrument.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: A notice says “Please mind the step by the gate.” What does “mind” mean on this notice?
questions.answer: Pay attention to the step so you do not trip.
options: Form an opinion about who built the step.
Look after the gate until someone returns.
Pay attention to the step so you do not trip.
Decide whether you object to the step.
questions.explanation: The notice warns readers to be careful near a change in floor level.

questions.subject: Verbal Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Use the surrounding words to distinguish meanings of words with the same spelling.
questions.prompt: “Ada’s aunt bought a new suit for the ceremony.” Which sentence uses “suit” as a verb rather than the name of clothing?
questions.answer: The later start will suit the visitors who travel by bus.
options: His suit has a pocket inside the jacket.
The navy suit was hanging near the door.
The tailor measured her for a suit.
The later start will suit the visitors who travel by bus.
questions.explanation: In “will suit”, the verb means to be convenient or suitable. All of the other examples use the clothing sense.
